title: Runbook + oncall enablement for Dedicated autoscaling bounds & predictive signals
creator: Talia Benson
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
Dedicated autoscaling is gaining new behaviors (hard min/max bounds, clamp reasons, predictive blending, feature-flag rollout). Oncall/SRE needs updated runbooks and training to safely operate the system, triage mis-scaling, and support customer escalations (e.g., stuck at min, throttling due to max, forecast failures).

Goal
1) Update and validate oncall runbooks for bounded autoscaling + predictive signals.
2) Enable SRE + infra oncall with drills/gameday and a signoff checklist before expanding rollout.
3) Align support escalation paths (macros/checklists) with oncall procedures.

Deliverables
A) Runbook updates
- Primary runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-dedicated-autoscaling-anomalies.json
  - Add new sections for bounds enforcement:
    - Recognizing clamp behavior vs actuation failure
    - clamp_reason taxonomy + how to interpret (min_bound, max_bound, cooldown_active, rate_limit, capacity_shortage, confidence_gated, safety_margin, drain_override)
    - “hard max” guarantee: what we do when demand exceeds max (throttle/queue, customer messaging, when to recommend increasing max)
  - Add predictive scaling failure modes:
    - Forecast service down / stale forecast / low confidence gating / feature anomalies
    - Graceful degradation expectations: revert to reactive signals; do not violate max; expect ramp lag
  - Add emergency actions:
    - Freeze autoscaling for a pool (pin replicas) + timeboxing guidance
    - Temporarily disable forecast input (feature flag) for a pool/region
    - Escalation criteria to Fleet Ops for capacity shortages

B) Oncall enablement checklist
- Create “readiness checklist” used as gate for staged rollout:
  - dashboards live (bound violations should be 0)
  - paging routes verified (ownership for forecast pipeline vs autoscaler controller)
  - runbook includes copy/paste queries for decision logs
  - access/RBAC validated for Console scaling history + internal tooling
  - support macros ready and linked (INT-1338)

C) Drills / gameday
- Execute the planned incident drills:
  - sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/autoscaling-incident-drills-gameday-plan.json
- Minimum scenarios:
  1) Sudden traffic spike with customer max bound causing throttling (expected: no max violation; customer comms; suggest max adjustment; confirm SLO impact and alert behavior)
  2) Forecast pipeline failure (expected: confidence gating triggers fallback; confirm alerts; no runaway overprovision)
  3) Cooldown + clamp interaction causing stuck behavior (validate hotfix behavior; ensure runbook points to symptoms + mitigation)

Scope notes
- This ticket is not implementing new autoscaling behavior; it is about operational readiness and training for the already-implemented features.

Acceptance criteria
- Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE + Infra (at least Rafael Mendes + Keiko Yamamoto signoff).
- Oncall training session completed (recording or written notes shared).
- Gameday completed with notes + action items filed as follow-ups.
- Rollout gate checklist completed for dogfood + design partner rollout.

Links
- Runbook (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-dedicated-autoscaling-anomalies.json
- SLOs/alerts doc: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-autoscaling-slos-and-alerts.json
- Observability PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-842.json
- Hotfix reference (cooldown/clamp interaction): sources/github/redwood/pr-22057.json
- Support readiness: sources/jira/internal-support/INT-1338.json

Owner/participants
- DRI: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Partners: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Keiko Yamamoto, Vanessa Ortiz, Dev Patel

Rollout gate
- Required before enabling bounded autoscaling for additional customers beyond allowlist (ENG-2848).
